comparison: Both evaluate identical claims (C2, C32-C38) about ERMES localization at division sites. OpenEval finds the imaging evidence strongly supportive, while Peer Reviewer 3 questions whether observed events represent actual division or merely tethered mitochondria breaking apart, requesting better visualization to clarify genuine division events.

Both evaluate identical claims (C39-C40) about Gem1 localization with ERMES subunits. Both assessments agree that the imaging data with functional GFP-tagged Gem1 supports these localization findings, with no concerns raised by peer reviewers.

Both evaluate overlapping claims about stable constrictions in gem1Δ cells (C3, C41-C49, C57, C64, plus C77-C78 in peer review). OpenEval finds comprehensive imaging evidence supports the model, while Peer Reviewer 4 questions whether observed sites are genuine constriction sites versus separate mitochondria with ER between them, affecting interpretation of Gem1's role.

Both evaluate identical claims (C50-C56) about structure-function analysis of Gem1 mutants. OpenEval finds the differential rescue data strongly supportive, while Peer Reviewer 2 requests additional experiments to determine if mutations rescue ERMES complex phenotypes, indicating the analysis needs further development.

Both evaluate identical claims (C58-C63) about ER-mitochondria contacts in gem1Δ cells from electron tomography. OpenEval finds the quantitative data supportive, while Peer Reviewer 5 identifies an apparent discrepancy with prior literature (Kornmann et al., 2011) regarding ERMES foci size and number, requesting clarification.

Both evaluate overlapping claims about nucleoid-ERMES association (C5, C6, C65-C67, plus C7 in peer review). OpenEval finds the imaging and quantitative data well-supported, while Peer Reviewer 1 states the role of Gem1 in mtDNA inheritance remains less developed and questions whether gem1Δ affects YME2-GFP distribution, requesting additional data.

Partial overlap on mammalian observations (C69-C70). OpenEval rates the overall model as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct mechanistic validation, while peer reviewers accept the mammalian cell observations and conservation inference without challenge, supporting the comparative significance.

Both address C73 about bacterial division mechanisms. OpenEval finds the comparative inference reasonable given available evidence, while Peer Reviewer 6 requests clarification on how the mitochondrial mechanism differs from the bacterial paradigm, indicating need for more explicit discussion.

Partial overlap on background claims about ER-associated mitochondrial division (C1, C12-C15). Both assessments agree these foundational observations are well-established and appropriately cited, with no challenges from reviewers.

Both evaluate overlapping background claims about ERMES composition and properties (C17-C24). Both assessments agree these literature-based claims are well-established and serve as appropriate background, with no reviewer challenges.

Partial overlap on background claims about Gem1 and gem1Δ phenotypes (C25-C27, C29-C31). Both assessments agree these foundational claims are well-supported by prior work and provide appropriate context, with reviewers focusing on extending rather than challenging these observations.

Both address evolutionary correlation between Miro and mtDNA (C71, C72 in OpenEval; C71-C72 in peer review). Both assessments support the comparative genomic analysis and correlation, though peer reviewers note the mechanistic connection needs further development.

OpenEval evaluates claims C74-C76 about ERMES mediating contact biogenesis as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct mechanistic evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific model.

OpenEval evaluates claims C77-C78, C84-C87 about temporal model and GTPase domain function as SUPPORTED by convergent evidence. While peer R3 includes C77-C78, the broader synthesis in R10 has no direct peer correspondence.

OpenEval evaluates claims C79-C83, C88 about Miro function across species and speculative hypothesis about motility defects as UNCERTAIN, requiring experimental validation in mammalian systems. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
